explanation.summary: You had a TIA, sometimes called a "mini-stroke." It happened because of a new heart rhythm problem called atrial fibrillation. For about 20 minutes you had weakness in your right arm and trouble speaking, but this went away completely, and your brain scan showed no lasting damage. You were started on a blood thinner to help prevent a future stroke.

m1.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth two times a day, at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM.
tips: Do not skip doses or stop taking it unless your doctor tells you to.

m2.what_for: to help control your heart rate
m2.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (25 mg) by mouth two times a day, at 8:00 AM and 8:00 PM.

m3.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (80 mg) by mouth once a day at bedtime, at 9:00 PM.
tips: Your dose was raised from 20 mg to 80 mg.

m4.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (500 mg) by mouth two times a day with breakfast and dinner, at 8:00 AM and 6:00 PM.
tips: Your dose was lowered from 1,000 mg because of how your kidneys are working.

m5.how_to_take: Take 1 tablet (5 mg) by mouth once a day, at 8:00 AM.

m6.how_to_take: Take 1 to 2 tablets (500 mg each) by mouth only when you need them for headache or pain. Do not take them more often than every 6 hours, and do not take more than 3,000 mg in one day.

m7.how_to_take: Stop taking aspirin (81 mg). Do not take it anymore.
tips: You are now taking apixaban, and taking both together raises your risk of bleeding.

m8.how_to_take: Stop taking ginkgo biloba. Do not take it anymore.
tips: It can raise your risk of bleeding when taken with apixaban.

signs: One side of your face is drooping.
Your arm or leg feels weak.
You have trouble speaking or understanding others.
You suddenly cannot see well.
You suddenly lose your balance.
You have a sudden, very bad headache.
You throw up blood, or your stool is black and tarry.
A nosebleed or bleeding gums that does not stop after 10 minutes.
Your urine turns pink or red.
You have bruises you cannot explain.
Your pulse on the home monitor is below 50 or above 120.

i1.text: Check your blood pressure and pulse every morning with your home monitor, and write the numbers down.

i2.text: Do not drive until your neurologist tells you it is okay.

i4.text: Take a walk every day, as much as you are able to.

a1.text: Go to Maplewood Outpatient Lab for a blood test to check your kidney function on October 28, 2026, any time between 7:00 AM and 5:00 PM.

a2.text: You have a neurology appointment with Dr. Rachel Kim on November 4, 2026, at 9:00 AM at Maplewood Neuroscience Center, 4th floor.

a3.text: You have a cardiology appointment with Dr. Samuel Osei on November 10, 2026, at 2:15 PM at the Heart and Vascular Center, 2nd floor. Bring your blood pressure log with you.

a4.text: The clinic will call you to set up your 14-day heart monitor test. No action is needed from you right now.

a5.text: Call your primary care doctor's office at (203) 555-0130 to make an appointment within 1 week.
